status: FROZEN before any rule is scored. Changes need an amendment with its reason, written before the affected numbers are seen.
requested_by: Omri 2026-09-29 ('try it, then explain'): after Step 454 found that under our answer-z q80 rule about 20% of every answer's steps are flagged (about 99% of clean answers get a flag) and that 0.0140 of the 0.0168 matched-rule gap to Qwen PRM is how many steps are flagged per answer, test label-free decision rules that let the number of flags vary per answer; Omri added (same day) the classic route: use the estimated sensitivity/specificity/prevalence (Dawid-Skene) to choose the threshold.
question: Keeping the frozen step scores and their within-answer ranking, does a label-free rule that decides how many steps to flag in each answer (including none) raise the official PRMScore over the frozen answer-z q80 rule, and does it stop flagging clean answers?
prior_work_checked: Inventory 2026-09-29: no experiment let the flag count vary per answer for our score on PRMBench, and none used un-normalized answer-level information or DS estimates to set it. Raw answer telemetry was used only for ProcessBench yes/no gates (Step 331: GMM 20.00 -> 31.16 at q0.3; tail15 gates). This stage does not repeat them.
access: Development evidence on the already-evaluated population (13,769 answers; PRMBench 6,969). Not untouched confirmation. Labels enter only the evaluation.

frozen_inputs.step_scores: S_equal (DS filter then plain average of the 11 surviving channels, stage B) from .worktrees/ssl-pseudolabel-residual-v1/results/expectation_realization_v1/run_20260927_stage_b/STEP_SCORES.npz (frozen; local)
frozen_inputs.frozen_thresholds: run_20260927_stage_b_thr/THRESHOLDS.json['S_equal'] (per fold; byte-identical re-run of the frozen stage B)
frozen_inputs.raw_channels: exactly as er_stage_b_run.py builds them before answer standardization: DERIVATIVE_CHANNELS.npz level (11) + CT7 profile chosen_token_z_despiked + DERIVATIVE_CHANNELS derivative of chosen_surprisal; survivors = all but energy_innovation and top50_js (the DS filter's choice in 5/5 folds). Label-free check done before this protocol: between-answer variance share 0.10-0.40 for the raw channels (realized_z 0.00: normalized within answer upstream).
frozen_inputs.population: step_evidence_v1 OOF_ANSWERS.csv / OOF_STEP_SCORES.npz; PRMBench metadata pickle from INPUT_FREEZE.json; official scorer spectral_utils.prmbench.prmbench_evaluate (depth-feature-fusion-v1)

folds: For evaluation fold k: calibration fold c = (k+1)%5, fit folds = the other three (the stage-B roles). Every quantity a rule learns for fold k (standardization statistics, DS estimates, thresholds) comes from fit or calibration rows of fold k, never from fold k.

rules.R0_frozen: REFERENCE. Flag a step iff answer-z(S) >= tau_S[k] (the saved stage-B threshold). Must reproduce PRMScore 0.6565188557935739.
rules.R1_global: Global-scale score G_k = mean over the 11 survivors of (raw_j - mu_kj) / sd_kj, with mu, sd over all fit-fold steps of fold k (PB+PRMB). Flag iff G_k >= tau_G[k] = 0.8 quantile of G_k over the PRMBench steps of fold c. Allocation and placement both from G.
rules.R2_allocate: PRIMARY. n_i = number of steps of answer i that R1 would flag; flag the n_i steps of answer i with the highest frozen S (ties: earlier step first). Placement stays the frozen within-answer ranking; only the count per answer changes.
rules.R3_ds_map: Global marks: for fold k, channel j is marked +1 at a step iff (raw_j - mu_kj)/sd_kj >= the 0.8 quantile of that channel over the fit-fold steps (else -1). Dawid-Skene (er_stage_a.em_estimate, kind 'ds', unchanged) fitted on the fit-fold marks gives psi_j, eta_j, prevalence pi. Posterior P(error | marks) in closed form; flag iff posterior > 0.5.
rules.R4_ds_expected_f1: Same DS model. For cutoffs c in the posterior quantiles 0.005..0.995 (step 0.005) of the PRMBench fit-fold steps, plus 0.5, compute the expected confusion on those steps with the posteriors as soft labels (expected TP = sum over steps kept valid of (1-p), FP = sum over kept of p, TN = sum over flagged of p, FN = sum over flagged of (1-p)) and the expected PRMScore; choose the maximizing c (ties: larger c). Flag iff posterior >= c. Label-free (controls are not identified; all PRMBench fit steps are used).
rules.R5_ds_count: Same DS model. n_i = round-half-up of the sum of posteriors over answer i's steps (capped at the answer length); flag the n_i steps with the highest frozen S (ties: earlier first).

primary_and_family: Primary contrast: R2 - R0 on official PRMScore. Confirmatory family: R1..R5 - R0 on PRMScore, Holm over the 5. A rule 'improves the decision' iff its Holm-adjusted 95% interval is entirely above 0.

endpoints.prmbench: official PRMScore (6,211 non-control answers), F1 on correct steps, F1 on error steps, recalls and precisions, flagged share of steps, correlation between each answer's flagged share and its error share (label-using diagnostic), share of erroneous answers with at least one error step flagged, within-answer AUC of the scale each rule places flags with (unchanged for R0, R2, R5)
endpoints.clean_answers: for the 758 controls (outside PRMScore, separate panel), the 160 multi_solutions and the 16 inert-annotation answers: share with at least one flag and step flag rate; RANDOM-SCORE BASELINE for every rule (LESSONS 2026-09-27): the same pipeline run on i.i.d. N(0,1) raw channels and scores, 3 draws
endpoints.processbench_secondary: official ProcessBench F1 per cell (predicted first error = first flagged step, -1 if none; accuracy on erroneous answers = exact first-error match, accuracy on correct answers = predicted -1; F1 = harmonic mean), macro over the 8 cells. The same frozen thresholds/models as PRMBench (tau calibrated on PRMBench steps); gate-free SLA (argmax) unchanged by construction

uncertainty: paired bootstrap over PRMBench source groups, 10,000 draws, seed 20261001; ProcessBench over PB source groups, 10,000 draws, seed 20261002; per-class breakdown of every rule vs R0 on the 9 official classes with Bonferroni-9 intervals (secondary)
nulls: for each rule vs R0 on PRMScore, 100 permutations each (decisions fixed, labels permuted): (A) labels permuted within each answer (keeps each answer's error count: an allocation gain SURVIVES this null by design and measures pure allocation; the residual measures placement), (B) each answer receives the label vector of another answer with the same step count in the same fold (keeps the length/position structure; a residual above 0 means the rule uses answer-specific information beyond length). Both reported with their interpretation.
hard_stops: R0 does not reproduce the frozen S_equal PRMScore to 1e-12
answer_standardize(raw)[:, survivors].mean(1) differs from the frozen S_equal by > 1e-9 on any step
a DS fit fails or returns a non-finite parameter; posterior not finite
any fold-k quantity computed with rows of fold k

predictions_frozen.P1: R1 and R2 flag at least one step in clearly fewer controls than R0 (< 90% vs about 99%)
predictions_frozen.P2: R2 improves PRMScore over R0 but by less than 0.0140 (the Step-454 allocation share of the PRM gap)
predictions_frozen.P3: R3 flags far more than 20% of steps (DS prevalence is overestimated, 0.22-0.41 vs 0.14) and loses on PRMScore
predictions_frozen.P4: R4 and R5 are closer to R0 than R3; sign uncertain
predictions_frozen.P5: on ProcessBench, R1 and R2 raise the official F1 over R0, because some correct answers get no flag

not_done: no change to step scores, channels, filter or weights; no threshold or quantile chosen from outcomes; only the declared 0.8 quantile (same as the frozen rule) and the declared DS rules; no new benchmark data
